note: Rejudged after 438bb234e4 changed handleLCPPacket's Code-Reject and Protocol-Reject handling (RXJ+/RXJ- by rejected Code or protocol, stopRejectedCode, lcpRejectFatalReason). Re-read Section 5.4: 'when a new Configure-Request is sent, it MUST NOT include any of the Configuration Options listed in the Configure-Reject.' The rejection flags sendConfigureRequest reads are still set in the unchanged Nak/Reject block, and a Configure-Reject never enters the Code-Reject branches; the new echo flags stopRejectedCode sets are read only by the echo ticker and the ser action, never by the request builder. The tagged units are unchanged. Server MRU-only rejection still keeps the other original bytes, and MRU/Auth/Magic rejection still yields an empty request that a valid Ack advances. The client MRU-only, Magic-only and all-option cases still assert the exact surviving bytes, an unchanged retransmission and no resurrection from later Nak suggestions. The IPCP DNS control still removes both DNS options, or Secondary-DNS alone, and learns no rejected DNS. Removal and preservation remain distinct assertions, so the verdict holds.
